construction_cost_boundary: All new U prices and fixed allowances are scenarios, not converted contemporary dollar quotations. Ordinary capital uses the existing economic allowance without adding its stock-times-price proxy.

Installed unit charges include fabrication, delivery/placement, supplier equipment, operation and capital recovery within their boundary. Supplier factories, freight fleets and generation capital are not added a second time.

The industrial-establishment increment covers extra regional mobilization, construction camps, commissioning and start-up losses above normal supplier capital recovery already included in installed charges. It is an unengineered allowance, not a second complete factory bill.
The qualification allowance is the incremental full-scale pressure/protection/repair/transition development programme beyond ordinary R&D. No revenue or residual asset sale offsets it.

The entire new regional infrastructure requirement and establishment increment are assigned to the first 100; future towns receive no advance allocation credit. Upstream industries must be orderable and charge attributable service/capacity; their civilization-wide creation is outside this estimate.

The ordinary-import freight increment is only the extra vacuum delivery burden above normal logistics in ordinary installed capital. Pressure, power and volatile imports are already delivered in their own rows.

Contingency applies once to direct construction. The separate removal reserve is 5% of direct construction, an initial funding allowance rather than a present engineering estimate or future recovery performance.

Cost excludes financing, migration fares, resident consumption and long-vacuum operation/renewal. Protective qualification and site clearance are conditions; allowances do not establish their success.

On-site material and road supplier prices exclude project-provided electricity and exterior cooling. Dedicated generation/beam hardware and radiators are capitalized here once; construction electricity adds only variable utility operating cost, with no second generation capital charge. Off-site manufacture and delivery remain inside their installed unit prices.
